title: The newest Bitcoin buyers are underwater

lines: Bitcoin's low on Nov. 15 — its weakest level in about four months.
By Wednesday morning it had climbed back to around $64,000.
But the slide left a mark.
People who bought in the last one to three months are now about 20% underwater.
They paid more than it's worth today.
Crypto now sits in spot ETFs and some retirement menus — in the US and Canada alike.
If crypto's in your long-term savings, size it so a 20% slide is survivable.
How much of your savings, if any, is in crypto?

caption:
Bitcoin just hit its lowest level since the summer — and the newest buyers are feeling it most.

It dipped near $61,000 on Nov. 15, a four-month low, before climbing back to around $64,000 Wednesday morning (CoinDesk). The catch: people who bought in the last one to three months are now about 20% underwater — they paid more than it's worth today.

Why it matters even if you don't trade crypto: it's crept into everyday savings now — spot Bitcoin ETFs and some retirement menus, in the US and Canada alike. A 20% drop there is real money, not a scoreboard.

Ether slid too, trading near $1,800.

My take: if crypto sits in your long-term savings, size it so a slide like this is survivable — the people hurting most bought recently and bought big.

How much of your savings, if any, is in crypto? 👇
